To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

aspirin is a safe and effective therapy for primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease and that the use of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs with aspirin may increase cardiovascular disease.

aspirin is the most effective and safe agent to reduce the risk of CVD in patients with rheuma-toid arthritis, and that NSAIDs, including COX-2 inhibitor, may reduce the beneficial effect of aspirin on CVD.

aspirin is a very useful drug for secondary prevention of CVD, but its use may be compromised by the concurrent administration of NSAIDs and that COX-2 selective inhibitors are less effective than NSAIDs in reducing joint pain and swelling in patients with rheumatic diseases.
